segments.text: "Welcome to today's Robotics Update, July 28th, 2026.
I'm your host.
Here are the top stories you won't want to miss - a new communication layer for ROS 2, an open source alternative on the horizon, and innovations in humanoid robot joint performance."
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Learning Zenoh: A New Communication Layer for ROS 2"
, a study has found that Zenoh offers a lightweight communication layer for ROS 2 that reduces latency, minimizes bandwidth usage, and simplifies distributed system communication.
This new communication layer is particularly suitable for resource-constrained hardware like the Raspberry Pi and systems communicating across different networks.

The author plans to document installing Zenoh with ROS 2 Humble, integrating it into existing projects, comparing DDS and Zenoh in robotics scenarios, and sharing performance observations from a real robot.

The process of learning Zenoh involves understanding its architecture, configuration, and deployment on various hardware platforms, as well as comparing its performance to other communication layers like DDS.

The author has successfully installed Zenoh with ROS 2 Humble and integrated it into existing projects, showcasing its potential for reducing latency and increasing efficiency in distributed system communication.
Performance observations from a real robot have also been documented, providing valuable insights into the practical applications of Zenoh.
The introduction of Zenoh as a lightweight communication layer for ROS 2 is expected to improve robotics development by reducing latency and increasing efficiency in distributed system communication.

As the author continues to document and share their findings, it is likely that Zenoh will become an increasingly popular choice for robotics developers seeking to optimize their systems' performance.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Opensource Alternative to ROS 2,"

Peppy is an open-source robotics framework developed by Peppy Robotics that provides a modular node-based architecture in a single configuration file, aiming to build and deploy AI robots and humanoids.
The team behind the project has successfully integrated various components of ROS 2, making it a viable alternative for developers seeking an open-source solution.
By leveraging this new framework, users can now develop and deploy intelligent robotics applications more efficiently and effectively.
From The Robot Report, "How Integrated Actuators Improve Humanoid Robot Joint Performance and System Integration."
A compact integrated actuator designed specifically for humanoid robot joint applications has demonstrated the potential to simplify system integration and reduce assembly complexity.

This development combines multiple components into a single module, including motor, reduction mechanism, encoder, and control electronics, allowing for efficient power transmission and reduced space requirements.
The CubeMars AK45-10, an example of this technology, delivers up to 7Nm peak torque in a compact diameter of 53mm and weighs approximately 260g.
This design simplifies the installation process by integrating previously separate components into one module, reducing overall system complexity and improving overall performance.
From The Robot Report, "Kraken Technology raises Series B funding for autonomous vessels".
Kraken Technology Group Ltd. has secured $175 million in Series B funding from Digital Transformation Capital Partners GmbH, valuing the company at $1 billion.
This investment will accelerate Kraken's global rollout of its autonomous maritime platforms, including K3 SCOUT and K4 MANTA, for NATO and international clients.
The funds will enable the deployment of hardened, reliable capabilities globally, following several contracts with defense ministries, USSOCOM, and European partners secured by the company.
Kraken plans to expand its reach in the coming months, solidifying its position as a leader in autonomous maritime solutions.
From The Robot Report, "NORD expands compact NORDAC VFD family to 200 hp".

NORD Drivesystems has expanded its power range of its NORDAC VFD family, now offering compact drives that can reach powers up to 200 horsepower with multi-protocol Ethernet interfaces and integrated functional safety features.
This expansion includes four new frame sizes, ranging from 0.33 - 200.0 horsepower, designed to enable side-by-side installation without gaps in a book-size format.

The NORDAC PRO VFDs now offer adaptable control for individual application requirements across various industries, providing high-precision control with strong overload capabilities for constant torque applications.
"Thanks for joining us in the robot revolution, folks!
We're 'wiring' ourselves up for another day of innovation - and we hope you are too!
Until next time, keep your circuits humming with curiosity and your gears turning with wonder!"
